summary: First comprehensive testing pass on Dompet K-eM (Indonesian UMKM finance copilot). Backend: 26/26 pytest tests pass (auth, business, dashboard, all 9 transaction types with side-effect verification, receivables, payables, products, reports, cross-business isolation, and AI assistant chat). Frontend: All pages load, all 7 record forms render with correct data-testids, AI assistant returns numerically-grounded Indonesian response citing exact Rp559.000 revenue matching /api/dashboard/summary, mobile viewport shows bottom-nav+FAB. HOWEVER, two significant bugs were found in the frontend integration layer: (1) BusinessContext loading race causing initial /dashboard visit to redirect to /onboarding even when user has an existing business, and (2) Receivables & Payables pages read `data.items` but the backend returns a plain array — so both pages incorrectly show empty state despite 10 open receivables and multiple payables in the seeded demo data.

minor.issue: Return a raw JSON array. Frontend expects wrapped {items, total_outstanding} object — API/UI contract mismatch. Either backend should wrap the response OR frontend hook/page should adapt. Only Reports uses the aging-shaped variant.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: On first load of any authenticated route (e.g. /dashboard), the user is wrongly redirected to /onboarding even when a business already exists. Root cause: refresh() does NOT setLoading(true) at the start when user transitions from null → authenticated, so AppShell renders with loading=false + business=null and Navigate('/onboarding') fires before the fetch completes. Fix: add `setLoading(true)` inside refresh() when user is truthy, before the api.get('/business') call. Reproduced 3x. Workaround used for further testing: navigate to /onboarding first, wait ~3s, then client-side pushState to /dashboard — dashboard then renders perfectly with full KPI data.

Reads `data?.items` and `data?.total_outstanding` but the backend GET /api/receivables returns a plain array. Result: page shows 'Total tertagih: Rp0' and empty-state 'Tidak ada piutang yang perlu ditagih' even though 10 open receivables exist and dashboard KPI card correctly shows Piutang Rp332.500. Same file useReceivablesOpen hook just returns res.data.
Same shape mismatch as Receivables — reads data.items / data.total_outstanding but backend returns array. Payables page will similarly appear empty despite seeded utang.
Accessibility warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined} for {DialogContent}' — cosmetic a11y warning, not blocking.

integration_issues.flow: Session cookie auth from browser (main-agent flagged as 'possibly 401 on /api/auth/me')
integration_issues.issue: NOT a bug — verified. Cookie auth works in real browser: GET /api/auth/me returns 200 with cookie session_token. The 401s the main agent saw are the initial pre-cookie /auth/me probe on the login page, which is expected behavior. Backend test test_me_cookie confirms.
See Receivables/Payables ui_bugs above — integration between /api/receivables|payables and page components is broken due to response shape mismatch.

action_items: FIX-1 (CRITICAL): In /app/frontend/src/context/BusinessContext.jsx refresh(), add `setLoading(true)` immediately before the `try { await api.get('/business') }` when user is truthy, so AppShell keeps rendering the loading spinner during the fetch and does not falsely redirect to /onboarding. Without this fix, ANY returning user hitting the root URL is dumped onto onboarding — this blocks basic app usage.

FIX-2 (HIGH): Reconcile response shape for /api/receivables and /api/payables. Either (a) update the endpoints to return {items: [...], total_outstanding: sum} OR (b) update Receivables.jsx / Payables.jsx / useReceivablesOpen / usePayablesOpen hooks to consume the raw array and compute total_outstanding on the client. Recommend (a) to match existing /api/reports/receivables aging shape.
FIX-3 (LOW): Add DialogDescription (or aria-describedby) to Radix DialogContent in record forms to silence the a11y console warning.

Once FIX-1 and FIX-2 land, main agent can smoke-test by (a) directly opening /dashboard with the seeded cookie and confirming no /onboarding redirect, and (b) opening /receivables and seeing the 10 items list.
critical_code_review_comments: BusinessContext.refresh() lacks setLoading(true) — classic React async guard mistake, leads to premature route decisions

API/UI contract mismatch on /api/receivables and /api/payables — response envelope is inconsistent with the aging endpoints; a stronger typed contract (or Pydantic response_model) would have caught this at build time

Backend CORS uses CORS_ORIGINS='*' with allow_credentials=True elsewhere would break withCredentials cookie flow across origins; not affecting current same-origin ingress but is a footgun if the frontend is ever hosted separately
Positive: server-side business_id resolution via get_current_business dependency is clean and prevents cross-tenant data leaks — verified with second-user isolation test

Positive: transaction_service.create_transaction/delete reversal maths verified end-to-end for SALE (paid+cash), SALE (unpaid → creates receivable), EXPENSE (cash reduction), TRANSFER (no profit impact), OWNER_WITHDRAWAL (cash-only, no profit impact) — all match expected

Frontend bugs to re-verify after fixes: (1) go straight to /dashboard with test_session_screenshot_tok cookie — must NOT redirect to /onboarding; (2) go to /receivables — must show 10 items list, not empty state; (3) same for /payables. Note: to avoid the pre-fix routing race during your own manual smoke test, land first on /onboarding, wait ~3s, then client-side navigate to /dashboard.

rca of the issue.onboarding_redirect_race: AuthContext initially has user=null while /api/auth/me is inflight. BusinessProvider's refresh() sees !user, immediately setLoading(false)+setBusiness(null). When AuthContext resolves user, refresh() runs again but never sets loading back to true, so AppShell renders in the tiny window between (a) BusinessProvider useCallback firing and (b) fetch completion — with loading=false and business=null → <Navigate to='/onboarding'>. The route change unmounts AppShell so the eventual setBusiness has no effect on routing. Reproduction: land on /dashboard with a valid cookie for a user who owns a business. Mitigation: `setLoading(true)` at the top of the user-truthy branch of refresh().
rca of the issue.receivables_payables_empty: Backend list endpoints return `List[Receivable]` directly, but the corresponding page components destructure `data.items` and `data.total_outstanding`. `undefined?.items` → falsy → empty state renders. Mitigation: wrap backend response OR adapt frontend hook to compute {items, total_outstanding} from the array.
